questions.q: A biomanufacturing facility upgrades its downstream purification hardware, resulting in the issuance of Revision 03 of the chromatography SOP. Under cGMP Document Control standards, what must explicitly happen to all physical laboratory copies of Revision 02?
options: They must be left in the active laboratory binders so technicians can compare the old method to the new method.
They must be gathered up, officially retired, and physically removed from active use to prevent accidental execution of the obsolete procedure.
They must be shipped directly to the regional EPA office for long-term copyright archiving.
They must be digitally scanned and posted to public scientific preprint servers for peer review.
questions.explain:
A critical tenet of **Document Control** is preventing the accidental use of obsolete, unapproved, or recalled procedures. 

When a new revision is issued (e.g., Revision 03), the Document Control unit must systematically retrieve and remove every single physical copy of Revision 02 from the active floor. The master copy of Revision 02 is stamped "OBSOLETE" and securely archived in a restricted QA vault for historical auditing purposes, while floor copies are typically shredded.

questions.q: Before a newly drafted Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) can transition from "Draft" status to "Effective" and be utilized on the manufacturing floor, it requires formal routing for signatures. Which internal department serves as the final authority, signing off to legally release the controlled document into circulation?
questions.explain:
In any regulated FDA/cGMP environment, the **Quality Assurance (QA)** department functions as the independent policing body of the facility. 

While subject matter experts in R&D or Manufacturing may *author* or technically *review* the document, QA holds the ultimate executive authority. QA's final signature verifies that the SOP complies with all federal regulations and internal quality policies before it is officially released for active use.

questions.q: To guarantee document integrity in the event that a multi-page SOP is dropped or pages are separated, controlled documentation standards require specific metadata to be printed on every single page (usually in the header or footer). Which combination of elements is mandatory for every page?
options: The author's home address, the facility's tax ID number, and the patent expiration date.
The unique Document ID number, the current Revision Level, and Pagination (e.g., Page 3 of 5).
A complete bibliography of scientific references and the exact GPS coordinates of the laboratory.
The CEO's digital signature, the annual corporate budget, and the daily timestamp.
questions.explain:
To maintain strict **Document Control**, an auditor (or technician) must be able to pick up a single stray piece of paper and immediately know exactly what it belongs to and whether it is complete. 

Therefore, every single page of a controlled SOP must display the **Document ID** (identifying the procedure), the **Revision Level** (proving it is the most current version), and strict **Pagination** (e.g., Page 3 of 5) to prove no pages are missing.
